$comment: SPEC §2.4 — no silent English fallback, ever. A key a component builds at runtime (`ui.module.${module}`) cannot be checked by reading the source, so every such template declares its domain here and scripts/i18n-lint.mjs expands it and verifies every resulting key exists in every catalog. A template found in app source with no entry here FAILS: an undeclared dynamic key is exactly how a missing translation reaches a user as a raw key.

ui.memory.type.${type}.$spec: §32.4 — the 11 memory types; sourced from the schema so the two cannot drift. They HAD drifted: this entry listed life_fact/relationship/goal/concern/health_context/belief_practice/important_date/language_style/conversation_thread, an eleven §32.4 does not contain, while the memory module carried the spec's own. Seven of eleven disagreed, and nothing failed because no screen had ever rendered a typed memory.

ui.module.${module}.$spec: §7.1/§34.3 — the 17 morning modules; sourced from the schema so the two cannot drift

ui.story.${state}.$spec: §25.5 — `none` renders no ring and needs no label

ui.tara.state.${state}.$spec: §4.3 — the 12 presence states; sourced from the schema for the same reason as the memory types. This entry listed warm_neutral/smile/full_smile/reading/safety — names §4.3 does not use — and omitted calm_guidance and encouragement entirely, so five of the twelve the API can serve had no alt text at all.

ui.kundli.graha.${g}.$spec: CC-007 KundliChart — the nine grahas, Rahu and Ketu included

ui.kundli.graha_short.${g}.$spec: §24.3/CC-007 — the glyph abbreviations inside the diagram's boxes

start.language.name.${code}.$spec: §10-3 — the eight language cards, each labelled in its own script

start.consent.item.${item.id}.label.$spec: §10-5 — essential, birth-data sensitivity, marketing (default off). Memory consent is DEFERRED to the first chip and voice consent to first voice use, so neither is a card here.

start.birth_time.option.${option}.$spec: §10-6 — the four honest options: exact / ±30min / part-of-day / unknown

start.interest.option.${option}.$spec: §10-8 — tunes Tara's register, never the facts; maps to profiles.density

start.priorities.option.${option}.$spec: §24.4 S11 — life priorities, at most three

start.reading.line.${line.id}.$spec: §24.4 S13. The API returns a line ID, never a message key — a server-supplied key cannot be verified by this gate, and the client must not render a string the catalogs never declared.

start.reading.observation.${line.house}.$spec: §0.17 — the minute-3 observation is house-specific so it is SPECIFIC; only the graha is a computed slot

start.reading.degraded.${degrade}.$spec: §24.6 — one honest line per degradation path, and the ceremony has exactly four

start.priorities.option.${priorities[0]}.$spec: §24.4 S11 — life priorities, at most three

journal.type.${type}.$spec: §30.5 — the five Journal artefact types; the closed set `journal/models.py` declares, so a sixth cannot be rendered without being added in both places

family.relation.${relation}.$spec: §32.15 — the closed relation set. A typed relation is a label in three locales; a free-text one is an English word in a Hindi sentence, which is why `Relation` is an enum at all.

reflection.prompt.${prompt}.$spec: §10-17 — three prompts as IDs, so Tara asks a Hindi user in Hindi rather than in a translated-at-render English question. The ORDER is served (`prompt_order`), never assumed from this list.

reflection.mood.${value}.$spec: §27 — five plain states and no numeric scale: a 1–10 slider on a bad night is a test she can fail

vault.source.${source}.$spec: §30.5 — deleting a conversation marks dependent memory sources "source removed"; the memory survives, its provenance does not
